strengths: Addresses an important question: which latent information multimodal contrastive learning can recover when modalities have distinct semantic and nuisance variables.
Reports encouraging gains from simple CLIP postprocessing across multiple backbones and datasets. For example, Table 2 improves ViT-B/16's average target accuracy from 32.51 to 37.13.

Includes synthetic experiments with assumption violations and three-run variability, plus ground-truth-factor evaluation on Multimodal3DIdent in Appendix P. These provide useful empirical observations beyond qualitative examples.
weaknesses: The central proof relies on a false optimality lemma. Appendix D.1, Lemma 2 claims that the normalized contrastive loss has global minimum zero. Under Eq. (4) on the unit circle with k = tau = 1, identity semantic encoders instead achieve approximately -0.421 for the intended cosine-distance objective. Moreover, its condition C1 requires identical embeddings for stochastic positive pairs; with the full-support vMF coupling and independent nuisance variables, this forces constant maps, contradicting the uniform-output condition C2. Both identifiability proofs depend on this lemma, leaving the main guarantees unsupported.

The convex-body argument has an additional substantive error. Appendix E uses an exactly uniform text marginal in Eq. (43), although Lemma 3 only supplies uniformity in the limit lambda approaching zero. At finite lambda, a truncated distance kernel generally produces a nonuniform marginal because its normalization depends on proximity to the boundary. Theorem 4.2 does not impose the required limit. Furthermore, Corollary 2 omits the non-Euclidean norm restriction introduced in Appendix E.2; arbitrary norms include the Euclidean case, where rotational ambiguity remains.

The claimed FastICA justification is incompatible with the spherical assumptions. Cartesian coordinates of a uniform hyperspherical variable are dependent, and rotational symmetry provides no identifiable ICA basis. The observation that the sphere has M-1 intrinsic dimensions does not establish independent sources recoverable through linear unmixing. The proposed PCA/local-isometry argument likewise does not establish that CLIP embeddings satisfy the convex-body recovery theorem.

The downstream experiments do not isolate disentanglement as the source of improvement. FastICA changes dimensionality and whitens features, but dimension-matched PCA and whitening-only controls are absent. A common orthogonal rotation preserves dot products and the optimum of an L2-regularized linear probe, making these controls particularly important. The reported gains therefore support useful feature preprocessing, but do not establish a benefit attributable to identifying independent components.

The 'beyond DAGs' contribution is insufficiently established. The assumed observational joint already factorizes as p(z_x)p(z_t|z_x), as used in the analysis. The paper provides neither sufficiently developed causal semantics for the undirected edge nor evidence that mixtures of opposing causal mechanisms satisfy its restrictive coupling distributions. Stronger recovery claims than prior work also depend on stronger distributional assumptions, so they cannot be attributed simply to relaxing DAG structure.

The recovery evaluation does not adequately substantiate component-wise identifiability. As specified in Appendix K, the synthetic R2 metric predicts learned representations from true factors; a high score does not rule out loss of latent dimensions. Appendix P supplies encouraging aggregate R2 results but lacks component-wise recovery comparisons and sufficient experimental detail. Selected CelebA traversals and downstream accuracy cannot resolve these limitations, and the main real-data comparisons omit uncertainty estimates.
